account: RL-Zero-Math's weight change (norm 4.12) acts through a low-rank core: per matrix its 8 largest singular directions (about 12 % of squared norm, as for any on-policy reward, LM-judge 0.127, against 0.030 for diffuse Think-SFT) read a residual subspace the base's own step-by-step text already drives 8-11x more than random and write directions the base's next layers amplify (1.67x), so base + 1.5x those directions matches RL (hard328 200.25 vs 200.0 right per sample of 328, MATH-500 456 vs 457) while random rank-8 edits of equal norm at scales -1 to 3 stay at the cued base (159-167 vs 164).

The change does two things the base already does on some of its own samples: it makes the answer open deliberatively and hold on after steps (mostly in the weights by RL step 100), and it lowers the per-step rate of one-off slips in every sample, so it adds right answers where the base already finishes (+13.5 points) and reproduces RL's outcome distribution rather than RL's per-problem outcomes; removing chance slips leaves each model's systematic wrong values, so the edit's wrong answers agree with RL's more than the base's do.

The three-token cue supplies the opening, since base answers that open deliberatively are right at the cued rate (-0.03), which takes MATH-500 from 224 to 410.5 of 500, within 1.4 points of RL step 100 at the same cap-hit rate and about 80 % of RL's gain, provided T 1.0 removes the T 0.6 loops (loop share 0.52-0.63 past 4,096 tokens) and the cap is long enough for the long right routes that a 4,096 cap cuts.

Steps 100 to 2,800 add the slip reduction (+42.5 of 500), and inference recovers only part of it: scattered base wrong answers (pair agreement 0.26) let a vote over 4 add 5-10 points for the base and step 100 against 2.9 for final RL, but on hard328 the base has no right sample on 26 of the 36 problems RL's vote wins, so the base's vote stays about 9.5 points (31 of 328) under RL's, while the 1.5x edit's vote ties RL's (+0.1) and the edit captures 0.88 of RL's per-sample advantage where the base has 0 of 4.

Forecast rule for edit cells (hard328, cue, one sample): the count is 164 + 39c, with c about 1 (RL's level, about 203, where it saturates) for Math-RL top-8 over all layers at 1x to 2x (Math 3.0 at 1x about 0.45); about 0.5 for any single part that keeps layers 0-21 (layers 0-10 or 11-21 alone, direction 1 alone at 1x to 1.5x, or directions 2-8), with parts nearly adding; about 0 for layers 22-31 alone, random rank-8, self-distilled LoRAs, IF-RL directions or tiny Think-SFT directions; and negative (140-168) for one band or one direction at 3x, -1x, or signed pieces; the vote over 4 of any c about 1 edit equals RL's (about 216 of 328).

Adding directions to a model already at RL's level changes nothing (RL + random 197, Think-SFT + 3x Math top-8 232 vs 230 alone), and on code RL-Code's own top-8 at 1.5x reaches RL-Code (399 vs 401 of 538, base 317), mostly on problems the base passes in other samples, while RL-Math's directions add only +1.5 pass points against Code's +7.0 because the rewards share the inputs that step-by-step text drives but each writes its own outputs.
